slides.notes: This presentation examines how LLMs can support the day-to-day work of an asset manager. It starts with peer practices, then develops proposed applications for the firm. The discussion follows front-, middle- and back-office work, using Company A and a quarterly client update as recurring examples. Cover image: an AI-generated research workspace.

shapes.name: !!scope.result
shapes.text: Build applications around the work people need to complete

slides.notes: The inputs are documents, data, messages and business requests. LLMs interpret questions, read and compare material, organize explanations, and draft text or code. Connected tools perform queries, calculations and other operations. Employees check the results and use them to complete research, trading preparation, client communications, review and development tasks.

slides.notes: The analyst needs to explain why Company A’s revenue grew and whether that growth can continue. The preparation involves locating comparable revenue and volume data, reading the explanation in meeting notes and comparing two research reports. In this illustrative scenario, prior-quarter and current-quarter revenue are RMB 100m and RMB 110m, while sales volume is 1.0m and 1.1m units. Repeated searches, extraction, calculations and rereading are the work required before the analyst can assess the business. The LLM organizes the questions and calls data and calculation tools. Those tools return the figures and calculations. The model connects them to operating and industry information, while the analyst assesses the quality and persistence of growth. Tianhong reported that the associated manual data preparation and calculations fell from days to minutes.

shapes.text: Start with research and client communications

shapes.text: Time spent preparing, searching and delivering

shapes.name: !!evaluation.1.body
shapes.text: Whether teams use the analysis and materials

shapes.name: !!evaluation.3.body
shapes.text: Whether employees continue to use the application

slides.notes: Start with research and client communications. Compare similar tasks before and after application use, tracking completion time, output adoption, rework and repeat usage. Use the findings to identify whether the issue is missing information, an unsuitable model explanation or an awkward query or file-handling step. Continued use and reduced preparation work provide a practical basis for deciding what to improve and extend.
